What kind of AI video do you need?

See stepsSee stepsSee steps

Choose by the shot you need to finish

Runway, Adobe Firefly and Luma are three starting points for short generated shots. Use the calculator below to check a selected model and allowance before subscribing. Test the same brief on your shortlist: a lower plan price does not establish better motion, consistency or usable output.

If you need a presenter reading a script or a finished social video with captions and music, first check a dedicated avatar or editing product. A five-second generated shot is only one part of that finished video.

  1. Write one brief: subject, action, framing, duration and target aspect ratio. Keep it unchanged between services.
  2. Choose the model and export settings in each service before comparing price. Do not compare credit counts across services without their per-generation costs.
  3. Download a trial result and check the actual file: identity, motion, unwanted text, audio, resolution and watermark. Then decide if another attempt is worth its displayed cost.

For image-to-video, start with the source frame

Choose a route that accepts a still image as a starting frame. Use a photo or illustration you have permission to upload. Keep the crop consistent and describe the movement you want, such as a slow camera push, rather than asking the model to redesign the subject.

Keep a small test: one input image, one motion brief and the shortest supported duration. Compare whether the subject retains its shape and whether the downloaded video fits your intended layout. If it changes important details, simplify the motion or try another model before buying a larger allowance.

The Luma example below is specifically a five-second Ray3.2 720p SDR generation with an image keyframe. Its price table adds 30 credits when there are no keyframes; higher resolutions and HDR also change the cost. The input and settings matter as much as the plan.

For text-to-video, separate scene creation from editing

Start with a single shot that describes one action. Plan a sequence as separate shots and verify each one before stitching them together. If a scene must preserve a specific product or character, compare a reference-image route as well.

Budget attempts rather than only final seconds. Three generated versions of one five-second shot consume three attempts even when you keep just one. Add your editing, voice and music needs separately; the calculator covers the generation allowance only.

Compare three starting plans

PlanListed allowanceExample setting
Runway Standard625 credits/monthGen-4.5: 60 credits per 5 seconds
Firefly Standard2,000 credits/monthUp to 20 five-second videos advertised
Luma Plus10,000 creditsRay3.2 720p SDR with keyframe: 100 credits per 5 seconds

These are different generation settings and models, so their capacity is not a quality comparison. Runway lists Standard at $15 monthly or $12/month with annual billing; Luma Plus lists $30 monthly or $300 paid yearly. Firefly Standard lists $9.99/month. Confirm the renewal price and billing period at checkout before committing.

Runway's free allocation is 125 one-time credits. Do not count it as a recurring monthly allowance. Firefly’s credits are shared with other premium features and reset monthly without rolling over. Reserve credits used elsewhere before budgeting video.

Will the allowance cover your planned clips?

Pick an example, then enter the number of finished clips and total attempts you expect for each one. The examples use five-second generations. You can replace the allowance and credits per attempt with the exact values shown in your chosen service.

“3 attempts” means one initial attempt and two retries. This is your planning assumption, not a measured success rate. Runway’s initial example needs 5 × 3 × 60 = 900 credits. With 625 available, it is 275 credits short and budgets three finished clips at that attempt count. Choose fewer clips, fewer attempts or a different setting before paying.

The Firefly example derives 100 credits per five-second attempt from its advertised 2,000-credit, 20-video maximum. It applies only to that advertised capacity; partner models and settings may cost differently. A budget fit does not guarantee enough usable clips.

Check a trial before choosing a paid plan

  • Subject: check hands, faces, logos and geometry over the whole clip.
  • Motion: compare the requested action with the exported result, including the first and last frames.
  • Delivery: check file resolution, duration, aspect ratio, watermark and whether required audio is present.
  • Rights and inputs: check the selected model’s current terms for the intended use. Confirm that you can upload the source image and publish the result.

If no output passes, keep the failed examples and change one variable: the brief, reference image or model. Avoid subscribing solely because a showcase clip looks good. If the short shot works but a full video does not, plan the edits and continuity checks separately.
